## Scope

Map ObServe 10.0 observations to ROS LL 4.2.0 O-INFO: one row per observed trip, with 24 fields.

See the [general export design](../export-design.html): select trip IDs first, then produce one workbook per trip.

This review separates source facts, Philippe's implementation and decisions needed for the new exporter.

This review combines source analysis with the frozen trip exports examined below.

## Database destination and import obligation

[Database review](../09-database-import/ll-database-import.html#o-info) records this sheet's tables and dependencies.

**Empty sheet, structurally: No for this trip export.** See the linked database review for the conditions.

## Confirmed source limitation: observer dates

ObServe records trip start and end dates, without separate observer embarkation and disembarkation dates.

This source limitation was confirmed during the design review on 12 November 2026.

`trip.startDate` and `trip.endDate` therefore describe the vessel trip, not independently recorded observer events.

The [official IOTC ROS-LL documentation][iotc-ros-ll] distinguishes O-INFO observation dates from V-TRIP vessel dates.

O-INFO describes the start and end of observations; both date-time fields are optional and expressed in UTC.

The official page was checked on 12 November 2026; it is a rolling `latest` reference, not a pinned model version.

Using the ObServe trip dates for O-INFO would be an explicit proxy assumption, not a direct source correspondence.

The preferred approach is to leave both optional O-INFO date-time fields empty because the source information is absent.

This is a provisional preference, not an approved mapping rule. The question remains open.

Do not substitute the vessel trip dates under this preference; retain them for the vessel-trip information.

[iotc-ros-ll]: https://data.iotc.org/reference/latest/forms/ros/Form-ROS-LL.html

## Input data and joins

The transformation uses `trip`, `activity` and `set`. Catch records are not needed for O-INFO.

| Starting field            | Reference table            | Values needed                          |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `trip.observer`           | `common.person`            | First name, last name and identifiers. |
| `trip.departureHarbour`   | `common.harbour`           | Port LOCODE and country ID.            |
| `trip.landingHarbour`     | `common.harbour`           | Port LOCODE and country ID.            |
| `harbour.country`         | `common.country`           | ISO3 country code.                     |
| `activity.vesselActivity` | `ll_common.vesselActivity` | Activity code and meaning.             |

Reference fields contain ObServe `topiaId` values. Catalogue lookups recover the corresponding records.

The observer must then be matched to the ROS observer registry to obtain an IOTC identifier.

Port and country values must match the ROS reference catalogues, including their canonical spelling.

`common.country` is reached through the harbour reference, not through a direct field of our four extracted sheets.

Reference preparation must therefore include this additional table when preparing O-INFO.

## Field mapping

The field names below are exactly those declared in the ROS LL 4.2.0 form model.

**Direct** means the source is identified. **Decision** means a reporting rule or additional information is required.

Mandatory status comes from `ros.form.model` 4.2.0. Resolve mandatory-field coverage first.

### Mandatory fields (4)

| ROS field                                               | Source                                                     | Mapping status                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `observed_trip_id`                                      | trip.topiaId; ROS identifier components to establish       | Decision: source ID does not satisfy the ROS trip-ID pattern.   |

| `observed_trip_summary_number_fishing_sets_conducted`   | activity and set records for this trip                     | Agreed: count distinct sets in FO activities.                   |
| `observed_trip_summary_number_fishing_sets_observed`    | activity and set records for this trip                     | Decision: establish the observation-coverage rule.              |

## What Philippe's SQL contributes

The query identifies the useful person, harbour and country joins and the `FO` activity-based counting approach.

Source: `sql-queries/observe_ll_trip.sql`, lines 18–31 and 65–76.

<details>
<summary>Relevant SQL excerpts</summary>

```sql
(ob.firstname || ' ' || ob.lastname)::text AS observer_full_name,
hec.iso3code::text AS embarkation_country,
he.locode::text AS embarkation_port,
he.latitude::numeric AS embarkation_latitude,
he.longitude::numeric AS embarkation_longitude,
t.startdate::date AS embarkation_date_time_gmt,
```

```sql
INNER JOIN common.person ob ON (t.observer = ob.topiaid)
INNER JOIN common.harbour he ON (t.departureharbour = he.topiaid)
INNER JOIN common.country hec ON (he.country = hec.topiaid)
INNER JOIN common.harbour hd ON (t.landingharbour = hd.topiaid)
INNER JOIN common.country hdc ON (hd.country = hdc.topiaid)
```

The conducted-set count is repeated unchanged for observed sets:

```sql
(SELECT count(a.topiaid)
 FROM ll_observation.activity a
 INNER JOIN ll_common.vesselactivity va ON (a.vesselactivity = va.topiaid)
 WHERE va.code LIKE 'FO' AND a.trip = t.topiaid)::integer AS number_of_sets_conducted
```

</details>

### Separate selection from extraction

Our export starts with a selected trip ID. O-INFO is built for that trip, as part of its own ROS workbook.

Philippe's query combines programme selection, reference joins and reporting calculations.

We reuse the identified source relationships, not that combined query structure.

Its inner joins can exclude trips with missing optional links. That is not our extraction convention.

Philippe uses the same FO activity count for both totals. The agreed rule below does not copy it to observed sets.

Source: `sql-queries/observe_ll_trip.sql`, lines 30–31 and 65–83.

### Reporting assumptions to resolve

* Harbour coordinates are assigned to fields that ROS identifies as embarkation or disembarkation **at sea**.
* Trip start and end dates are used as observer embarkation and disembarkation dates.
* Lost days are set to zero; the four reasons are left empty.

Source: `sql-queries/observe_ll_trip.sql`, lines 20–40.

These assignments are visible in the code. Their validity depends on the reporting meaning and source coverage.

## What Philippe's R code adds

| Operation             | Existing behaviour                                               | Decision for the new exporter                          |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Observer matching     | Remove accents, join on full name, use IOTCROSXXXX if unmatched. | Resolve one registry record; do not invent an IOTC ID. |
| Port formatting       | Insert a space after the first two LOCODE characters.            | Resolve against the ROS port catalogue.                |
| Observer date-times   | Append 00:00:01 and 23:59:59 to the trip dates.                  | Establish how unknown times are represented.           |
| Searching days        | Calculate trip duration, clipped to the reporting year.          | Determine whether events identify searching.           |
| Actively fishing days | Copy the number of conducted sets.                               | Define duration; do not assume one set per day.        |

Source: `r-script/ros_ll_iotc_v2.1.R`, lines 108–137.

The observer name join can multiply trip rows if the reference contains several matching names.

The date-time conversion does not specify a timezone in these statements.

<details>
<summary>R date-time and fishing-day assignments</summary>

```r
mutate(embarkation_date_time_gmt = as.POSIXct(paste(embarkation_date_time_gmt, "00:00:01")),
       disembarkation_date_time_gmt = as.POSIXct(paste(disembarkation_date_time_gmt, "23:59:59")))
```

```r
mutate(number_of_days_actively_fishing = number_of_sets_conducted)
```

These excerpts reproduce the existing code; they are not proposed implementation examples.

</details>

## Important ObServe distinction

`ll_observation.fishingSet.monitored` means **equipped with hook timers**, not **observed by an observer**.

Source: `observe-app/core/services/i18n/src/main/i18n/translations/services_en_GB.properties`, key below.

```text
observe.data.ll.observation.FishingSet.monitored=Equipped with hook timers
```

It must not be used as the observed-set counter without changing its meaning.

## Consequences for the intermediate model

O-INFO needs reference enrichment and trip-level summaries, not a new hierarchy of intermediate data tables.

The four-sheet approach remains suitable for this sheet, subject to resolving the reporting decisions above.

* Preserve the source trip ID; create the ROS trip ID once and reuse it across ROS sheets.
* Load person and harbour records by their ObServe IDs, with the countries required by those harbours.
* Match the observer, ports and countries to the ROS references.
* Count distinct sets for the conducted total; resolve observation coverage and activity-duration rules separately.
* Leave unavailable optional information empty unless an explicit reporting rule says otherwise.

The intermediate structure does not create the ambiguity about dates, observation coverage or activity durations.

Those decisions would also be necessary if SQL wrote O-INFO directly.

## Decisions before implementation

1. How is the ObServe observer linked reliably to one ROS observer, and how is the ROS trip ID constructed?
2. When can trip departure and return represent observer embarkation and disembarkation, including unknown times?
3. Which source records identify observed sets and establish each reported activity duration?

A development comparison should retain trip IDs and source records so each resulting O-INFO row can be explained.

## Working analysis: exportable data without assumptions

This is a proposed scope based on recorded facts and justified conversions. Existing decisions above still apply.

The live-data check below measures this selection. Missing required values and reporting rules remain unresolved.

### What can be populated

* Assemble the recorded observer name and retain the source trip/observer links.
* Use an IOTC observer ID only after an unambiguous registry match.
* Count distinct FishingSet IDs for the selected trip, restricting their activities to VesselActivity code FO.

### What stays unresolved

* Establish the ROS trip-ID rule and how to identify sets observed by the observer.
* Leave observer dates and embarkation/disembarkation locations empty without observer-specific evidence.
* Vessel trip ports and dates do not establish the observer's own movements.
* Leave activity-day totals and lost-day reasons empty until actual events support the requested measures.

`monitored` means equipped with hook timers; it cannot identify sets observed by a person.

### Complete-row assessment

The ROS trip ID, registry identity and observed-set count remain unresolved; O-INFO is not yet a complete row.

## Live-data check: 2025 selection

[Measured scope and evidence](ll-live-data-coverage.html): 67 trips, 461 sets and 8,703 catch rows.

The scope includes 17 observer-monitored trips and 50 self-reporting trips. These are different collection methods.

* All 67 trips have an observer link. The scope contains 17 OB trips and 50 SR trips.
* Their 461 sets are source records; they are not automatically counts of operations observed by a person.
* Observation method is recorded, but neither OB nor SR by itself supplies a ROS sampling or coverage rule.
* IOTC observer matching and observer-specific movement information remain unresolved.


## Measured coverage: observer trips, 2020–2025

Checked on 13 November 2026 against the frozen export `20261112T221530Z` and ROS LL form model 4.2.0.

This cohort contains 70 OB trips. The preceding 2025 analysis includes self-reporting trips and has a different scope.

| Mandatory ROS field                                 | Recorded source coverage                   | Remaining decision                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| observed_trip_id                                    | trip.topiaId present in 70/70 trips        | Define the ROS ID construction rule.          |
| observer_identification_iotc_id                     | Observer links present in 70/70 trips      | Map 15 ObServe people to ROS observer IDs.    |
| observed_trip_summary_number_fishing_sets_conducted | 700 set records across 70/70 trips         | Agreed: distinct set IDs, FO activities.      |
| observed_trip_summary_number_fishing_sets_observed  | The same 700 records are source candidates | Confirm which operations were observed.       |

All 15 observer IDs resolve in the frozen ObServe person catalogue, with first and last names present.

This confirms source identity availability; it does not confirm any match to the ROS observer registry.

All 700 activity records have code FO (fishing operation), and each has one linked set record.

There are no activities without a set in this cohort. Each trip contains between 1 and 32 recorded sets.

| Year | Trips | Recorded sets |
| ---- | ----- | ------------- |
| 2020 | 8     | 73            |
| 2021 | 13    | 120           |
| 2022 | 7     | 92            |
| 2023 | 12    | 137           |
| 2024 | 13    | 131           |
| 2025 | 17    | 147           |

Counting source rows is reproducible. Using that count as conducted sets is the reporting rule agreed below.

Neither the trip method OB nor the hook-timer flag establishes complete observation coverage by itself.

No ROS identifier mapping or set-count rule was implemented during this review.

Evidence: yearly trips.csv and files.csv indexes, and trip.csv, activity.csv and set.csv in each trip folder.

Reference checks use common.person and ll_common.vesselactivity from ObServe catalogue snapshot 20261112T184113Z.


## Agreed set-count rule — 13 November 2026

For conducted sets, count distinct ll_observation.fishingSet.topiaId values belonging to the selected trip.

Include only sets whose activity references a ll_common.vesselActivity record with code FO (fishing operation).

Join activity.vesselActivity to vesselActivity.topiaId and apply vesselActivity.code = 'FO'.

Philippe counts FO activities. This rule counts distinct sets linked to those activities.

The counts coincide for the 70 exported trips: all 700 FO activities have exactly one set.

Follow fishingSet.activity → activity.topiaId → activity.trip; use the same selected trip ID as every source query.

This rule treats the recorded set list as the conducted-set total. It does not independently prove source completeness.

The observed-set count remains unknown pending confirmation that unobserved sets can or cannot be recorded here.

Do not copy the conducted count, substitute zero, or use monitored: that field means hook-timer equipment.

The field is a mandatory integer. Unknown is a review status; no accepted ROS value or failure policy is chosen yet.

This records the agreed reporting decision. No extraction or transformation code was changed.
